reviews.author: Jenna
reviews.text:
It was the most delicious sushi I've ever had. I mainly eat salmon while living abroad, and I was surprised at how delicious it was, making me wonder if this is what the salmon I used to taste like.

When I go out to eat sushi, I don't usually eat egg sushi because it's obvious, but after eating it at Kita Sushi, I thought it would be delicious to eat at a good restaurant.

I went right at opening time and sat down and ate comfortably without waiting. After going to Kida Sushi, I came back overseas and went to two or three other sushi restaurants, but Kida Sushi is the only one that comes to mind.

reviews.author: manul garlic
reviews.text: Rather than being a sushi restaurant, Kida Sushi is famous as a place where you can enjoy good value for money sushi in Itaewon. This is a sushi restaurant in Itaewon that is already known to boast a long history. The interior is small, so you have to wait a lot. Lunch sushi, which can be eaten inexpensively for lunch, is popular. In addition to sushi, you can also taste a variety of sashimi. What can be said to be a characteristic of ‘Kida Sushi’ is that the ratio of rice to fish is a little different from other sushi restaurants. It is said that customers who visit the store once cannot forget the taste and come back again because the rice is small and the fish is large, so it has a unique chewy taste in the mouth and a special texture. The menu that the Kidasushi chef is most proud of is the salmon roll. Usually, sushi rolls have a lot of rice, but the 'Gida Sushi' salmon roll has less rice and is filled with salad. The combination of the crunchy texture and soft salmon is excellent, and it is sprinkled with plenty of tartar sauce, making it a perfect combination.

reviews.author: Jang Mi-ri
reviews.text:
I came here for work nearby and came to visit.
I heard that the water type is delicious, but as rumored, the roll is even more delicious. I visited during peak lunch hour and it wasn't full, but it took a while for the food to come out. Weekday lunch sushi is available at a low price that is hard to find in the area, and the sushi is served with warm somen as well. I don't think you should expect as much quality as the price. The roll was full of shredded cabbage, crab meat, pickled radish, etc., so it was crunchy and the portion was generous!! It's good value for money, but I don't think I'll ever visit again.

reviews.author: Narae Kim
reviews.text: The food is always delicious and fresh. The downside is that there is a bit of a wait, but the longer you wait, the better it tastes! Oh, and it depends on what you think, but the price is not cheap. The transportation isn't very good, but I never felt any inconvenience, so I passed. reviews.author: Seokjun Yoon
reviews.text:
I was a little hesitant because the previous review mentioned hygiene, but it didn't feel particularly dirty or bad.
By mixing it with fish broth, it brings out the unique savory taste, and by adding a little spiciness, it also takes away the greasiness of the pork broth.
It's oily and salty, so there may be some people who like it or not, but I'm personally very satisfied.
Anyone who likes local ramen will like it.

reviews.author: Lee So-eun
reviews.text: There are a lot of flies and the hygiene is a bit bad. I ordered Daechang Ramen and regular shoyu ramen, but they were average. I recommend just shoyu ramen and spicy rather than Daechang. I happened to go there while passing by because other restaurants were on break, but it's a ramen restaurant nearby that's not bad for just a meal.

A hidden restaurant. I only thought it was shoyu-based, but it has a subtle niboshi mel... It's niboshi ramen.
The broth has an appropriate salinity to suit Korean tastes and is lighter than Japanese style. it's good.
The chashu is surprisingly tender and more appetizing than I expected.
I'm glad that I found a good restaurant again after a long time.

reviews.author: Dongchan Seo
reviews.text:
It's the kind of taste you want to eat on a cold day when you crave warm ramen soup. The main menu the owner recommended was shoyu ramen, but he also recommended Korean beef daechang.
.
I decided to try Korean beef Daechang ramen. Actually, I don't really like foods like makchang, daechang, and giblets, but I liked the Daechang ramen here.
.

Not only did I not feel it, but my mouth was filled with a savory taste.

The staff also seemed to work with pride.

Due to the fact that the store is located in a semi-basement area, the bathroom may be a bit poor.

reviews.author: ramen master
reviews.text:
Hanataka Ramen located in an alley in Itaewon.
Itaewon was severely empty due to the aftermath of the coronavirus, and most of the businesses, including this place, were empty.
Even though it was lunch time, it looked very leisurely.
It may be everyone's wish, but I hope the coronavirus disappears quickly.
Because I had no information about the business before visiting.
With zero expectations, I was weighing whether to eat Daechang or Shoyu. I thought it would be better to go with the basics, so I ordered Shoyu.
There were no guests other than me.
After about 10 minutes, shoyu ramen came out.
I quickly took a few pictures and took a sip of the soup.
It was a taste that made my eyes sparkle.
It was a soup with a very strong Kyokai flavor.
The medium-thick noodles were soft and strong and went really well with this soup.
I was satisfied with everything in this bowl, including the chashu and the eggs that looked like soybean paste.

reviews.author: Seo Sanghyuk
reviews.text:
Maze soba, gochujang soft tofu udon, and fried chicken
Korean-Japanese fusion cuisine with a slightly Chinese style

It's the first time I've tasted the rich taste of udon soup. Water parsley goes well with it too.

Overall, it was so special that I ate it with full concentration.
The only downside is that it is small, so I wonder if I can bring my wife and baby to eat there later.

reviews.author: Anrak Kim
reviews.text:
A small restaurant located in an alley near Hangangjin. This place has a variety of vegan options. They sell vegan gelato. They seem to sell a lot of simple meals such as sandwiches during the day, and food that can be used as drinks or snacks at night.
The atmosphere of the store is cozy and pretty. It feels like they put a lot of thought into things like lighting and furniture. The downside is that there are not many seats inside, and the space is small, so it is a bit noisy.
I ordered a sandwich and soup, and it was cooked with focaccia made from rice. The bread was fluffy and went well with soup and sandwiches. However, it was disappointing that the sandwich ingredients felt overly seasoned. The soup was warm, quite large, and very tasty.
The intention to revisit is average. Itaewon has many vegan restaurants, and the overall visiting experience was not excellent due to the staff's service. There were many people who only packaged gelato.

reviews.author: Seokmin Jin
reviews.text: I went right after the coronavirus and visited again after a long time. If you just forget about the price and eat it, it's great. reviews.author: Belle Park

Each dish was excellent and perfect. Dajung was dancing with her ingredients and each of them was just as good as her performance. I would recommend to go alone or two to just be submerged and be one with the chef.
They remembered my birthday (by overhearing at the reservation) and gave me the most memorable gift and experience with the fine dining.
Thank you Lee
Dajung and Sebastian!
See you soon!

Chef Dajeong's every movement seemed like she was dancing, it was like watching art. It was a dining experience that satisfied all five senses. I recommend going alone. I hope you put down your phone and have an experience that focuses solely on the chef, ingredients, and taste. It was a lasting impression.

reviews.text: A Teppanyaki restaurant located in a wonderful space called Hyatt. Unfortunately, compared to the price, the satisfaction level of the food was quite disappointing. The wine pairing was so disappointing that it made me shake my head.

reviews.author: Sam Hahn

Fine dining under the guise of Teppanyaki. Quite French in terms of sauces. Endives, quinoa, etc. are used as substitute ingredients to cleverly demonstrate that the combination and taste are similar. It seems like there are a hundred different ingredients...

The perfect place for a quick second round of Club Lounge Happy Hour.

I recommend going with 2 to 4 people rather than multiple people.
Not noisy, perfect for conversation

A completely different atmosphere from Itaewon.
But the taste is just like Itaewon~
The oyster jjamppong is especially impressive.
There are times when it feels a little salty, but it's more salty than bland.. haha

Rating: 👍👍👍👍
Place: Hannam-dong Number One Lamb Skewers

A Chinese restaurant located at Hannam Intersection.

This is a very popular restaurant that was introduced on Sung Si-kyung's YouTube channel. You can enjoy Chinese food with a menu that makes you feel like you're in real China, different from typical Korean-style Chinese restaurants.

This is a restaurant where every dish shows a lot of potency, and in particular, Hyangnayukseul is the best side dish that made even me, who doesn't really enjoy cilantro, fall in love with the refreshing charm of cilantro.

Number Won Yang Galbi is different from traditional lamb skewers in that you can eat the meat attached to the thick rib bone on a skewer, making it a great menu to experience the essence of real lamb.

The eggplant dish was just ok, and the Hwangjinwimi, a crazy carbohydrate bomb similar to junk food, is a secret dish of this house, with corn that explodes in your mouth and has a sweet taste that leads you to pork as a side drink.

The highlight of the day was a Chinese liquor called ‘Janggunwang’. Even though it was 52 percent, it didn’t have any of the burning sensation that comes after eating Godosu’s Pegal, and it went down so smoothly that I almost went to hell after continuing to drink it.

This house is quite dangerous, so it is recommended that you be especially careful and try it on a day when you are likely to break it or have an accident.

Review for Koreans: One of the few places in Seoul where you can get Pakistani food. I visited for a late lunch on a Saturday, and the kitchen was manned by a male owner. Oh, you can order in Korean.

Ordered mutton karahi, nihari, logni naan, rice, and 2 cups of milk tea.

Mutton Karahi is stir-fried with tomatoes, peppers, and onions to make it sweet and spicy, and seems to be perfect for Korean tastes. The nihari must have been made from beef shanks, so there were some parts that were rough and some meat attached to the bones. The group said that Karahi was more delicious, perhaps because it was less spicy and had an emphasis on salty taste compared to Karahi. To my taste, Karahi was good with naan and Nihari was good with rice.

Rogni naan is a thick butter naan with sesame seeds sprinkled on top, and because it is quite thick, I felt full with just one piece. The rice is long-grain rice and the quantity is generous. Milk tea is exactly what is commonly called chai.

All in all, it came to a little less than 40,000 won, so I think I'll stop by often to eat Pakistani-style food that I don't often get to eat.

For foreigners: Recommend to those who want Pakistani cuisine, which is hardly found in Seoul. Owner is very very gentle, food was great(although I am not sure it is authentic or not, I haven't been to Pakistan yet) and price was reasonable. Ordered mutton karahi, nihari, roghni naan, rice and milk tea, none of them disappointed me. Long long review above is for domestic customers who have little experience on Pak-Indian food.

reviews.author: Lim Jeong-hyeon
reviews.text:
Dreamy Thai taste that fills the night in Hannam-dong, Michelin 2025 ‘Yuhan’
Title: A visit to 'Yuhan', a Thai bistro in Hannam-dong, a place that only I wanted to know about but has already become famous
In Hannam-dong, a fierce battleground for gastronomy, there is ‘YOUHAN’ with an impressive red logo inside a quiet alley leading to the embassy. In fact, this place was popular among gourmets, and its true value was recognized by being proudly named in the 'Michelin Guide Seoul 2025'. Reservations were fierce even before the Bib Gourmand badge was attached, so I visited with high expectations.
1. Atmosphere: Exotic mood blooming in the dark
The moment you open the store door and enter, the noise of Seoul is blocked out and you feel like you are in a hip speakeasy bar in Bangkok. The overall dark interior with reduced lighting is dreamy and calm. The heat emanating from the open kitchen, the intermittent sound of the wok, and the faint scent of spices stimulate the appetite. The tables are spaced appropriately and the lighting is set to focus on the food and the other person, making it the perfect choice for a blind date or date.
2. Taste: Uncompromising balance of spices
Befitting its identity as a 'Thai bistro', the food here is different from the taste of typical Thai restaurants.
The most impressive thing is the use of spices. Rather than compromising to suit Korean tastes, we boldly used strong local herbs and spices from Thailand and refined them so that they can be paired with wine.
The grilled food, filled with the scent of charcoal fire, was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, making it fun to chew, and the curry had a great spicy kick behind the softness of the coconut milk. Each dish tastes like wine.
3. Pairing: A mariage of Thai food and wine
Yuhan’s real charm comes from its mainstream list. It's usually easy to think of beer when it comes to Thai food, but the wine list here is quite extensive. From natural wines to conventional wines, the lineup of alcoholic beverages to balance the spicy and sour Thai cuisine is excellent. The recommended white wine went perfectly with the acidity of the chili and lime sauce.
4. Service and overall review
As expected from a business selected by the Michelin Guide, the hospitality was minimal. The explanation of the menu was friendly, and the food came out at a reasonable speed. 'Yuhan' is not just a restaurant to fill your stomach, but a place that sells an 'experience' that combines space, taste, and alcohol.
If you see a sign with red letters at the entrance to an alley in Hannam-dong, I recommend going in without hesitation. It may be harder to make a reservation now, but it is well worth the trouble. You will be able to see at the tip of your tongue why Michelin chose it in 2025.

When it comes to cocktails, mango is better than coconut. The coconut was a bit watery and fishy. The mango is more like a juice than a cocktail. There was too much ice, so it melted and the cocktail turned to mush, so I had both left. I think it would be better to order wine.
Saiua goes well with spices, the scent spreads gently in your mouth, and it tastes like high-quality ham. In fact, it was a dish that was closer to a patty and had fluffy meat particles.
Keang Kiao Wan was the most delicious dish I had here. This is a great curry restaurant. The curry with rich spices captured my taste buds.
Tetmankung tasted like a croquette with light vegetables and shrimp. The sauce was not spicy and mayonnaise-flavored, and I recommend it if you like something mild. It was edible, but not delicious. It would have been better if the temperature had been warmer. It was disappointing that it came out cold. Aside from the curry, the food and drinks were all poorly seasoned.
The satay was a great combination of pineapple and meat. The juice from the pineapple bursting out was like meat juice, so it was delicious.
Khao Niao Mamuang was a top secret for me. It tasted shocking and honestly, it was a bit horrible. It was a combination of glutinous rice soaked in coconut milk, a mango syrup-flavored sauce, and ice cream, but it was just like eating glutinous rice with mango syrup and ice cream. reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
I already knew that it was an expensive neighborhood.
Still, I had a strong memory of being “priced but shocked by the new taste” at Kin Khao in San Francisco a long time ago, so I visited with the expectation that “I could taste unique Thai cuisine even if it was a little expensive.”
To conclude, I did not experience the strangeness and fun I felt in Kin Khao this time.

The first dish is som tam (23,000 won).
The menu had ‘Seasonal Chodang Corn and Jeju Carrots’ written in large letters, and the server also emphasized that point twice.
The corn kernels were sweet, but after moving my chopsticks a few times, the thought occurred to me, “For this price, there has to be something special about it, but isn’t this just an average salad?”
When I searched online reviews, I saw a lot of positive reviews saying “the vegetables are fresh,” but honestly, isn’t freshness the default?

The second is Kai Chau Goong Sam Lot (22,000 won).
The red sauce (Ssam Lot), which is said to have ‘three flavors’, is definitely delicious.
There were layers of sweet, sour, and spicy, but when I took another bite, it felt like high-end Sriracha.
The problem is the presence of crab meat and shrimp that were said to fill the stomach.
The shrimp are bite-sized and the snow crab meat is about ‘there.’
The omelette itself didn't feel much different from the Korean-style steamed egg custard, so I don't know where to find the charm of the Thai-style omelette.

Lastly, I ordered pot seed with or without pot (26,000 won).
It was interesting that they used short noodles instead of long rice noodles.
However, as soon as the soy sauce base flavor touched my mouth, I had a strong feeling of déjà vu, “Oh, is this the soy sauce flavor of royal tteokbokki that was popular in the past?”
Although there was a large amount of meat, it was difficult to call it a ‘good part’, and the shrimp felt like they were innocently stir-fried shrimp, but they were wrong.
Instead of the “Thai style salty + fiery taste” that should be fresh in the mouth, the familiar soy sauce stir-fry remains, so the novelty is lost.

The mainstream story cannot be left out.
In this house, ‘one glass of alcoholic beverages per person’ is required.
However, as soon as I opened the door, the strong smell of spices made me lose any desire to look at the wine list.
The environment is unfavorable for enjoying scents in the first place.
So I chose Sixton Piculier, a British IPA bottled beer (I saw it for the first time and ordered it).
The price (15,000 won) was good compared to the menu, but a place with interior design and price range like this should have at least a draft beer tap.
It's a shame that they only have bottled beer.

The service and atmosphere have both ‘Michelin’-like advantages and ‘Bib Gourmand’-like disadvantages.
The server kindly explains the production area and recipe for each menu, but the spacing between the tables is narrow and the ceiling is low, so the explanation is half lost when the sound of conversation from the table next to you mixes with it.
If you look at reviews, there are many people who say, “The atmosphere is great,” but honestly, the noise and density are closer to “good but inconvenient.”
Moreover, it is difficult to erase the feeling that the explanation price is about 5,000 won per menu.

In the end, my thoughts after receiving the bill were simple.
If the price were cut in half, I would frequent this ‘good value Korean-style Thai restaurant’, but at the current price, today might be the last time.
As much as I expected something new, I was disappointed.
Excessively Koreanized taste, fancy sauce plating, and poor liquor lineup.
If you are looking for “moderately expensive yet unique Thai food” in Hannam-dong, Yuhan unfortunately does not fill that role.

As the name Brooklyn suggests, it is impressive that red bricks were used as the identity of the restaurant building, and the food and red bricks match well in that pizza is made in an oven.
Each table is equipped with a kiosk.
The first floor is a space for making pizza, and you can eat on the second and third floors.
Most of the clerks are foreigners of Arab or Indian descent.
I didn't feel like the service was that good (especially the Korean female clerk).
Also, I felt like it would be difficult for two people to order pizza at a table for two because the table was too small. It was uncomfortable.

Store & Tips & Review

You order and pay at the kiosk in front of the store, and receive your food at the pickup zone on the right.

I heard it was a Michelin-starred Italian restaurant, so I made a reservation and visited on a weekday.
First of all, bread and dishes were served before the meal, and although the bread was dry, it tasted healthy. It can be refilled.
The menus came out one after another, and it took a long time for each menu to appear.
The main dish, the Iberico Grill, where the Italian chef personally opens the pork lid. The pork plate with grilled pork belly in Korean, very delicious roast potatoes, grilled onions, and sprout salad was the best. I can't believe the pork belly is so soft and tasty...
Caldaro, a signature menu item filled with various seafood, is a delicious crab stew itself.
Just like the company name ‘Borgo’, which means ‘neighborhood’, each and every dish tastes simple and friendly, without being overly spicy, like home-cooked Italian food.
After a satisfying meal, there was fruit wine and homemade chocolate dessert.
Every time the menu changes, the staff uses new utensils to serve you.

The staff are so friendly.
Even during meals, the staff closely observed(?) to see if anything was needed, and took turns taking group photos when the main dishes were served. It was touching.

reviews.author: YeonSoo Noh
reviews.text:
I visited this Michelin-starred Italian restaurant. It's in Hannam, so it's hard to find because there's no sign, but it's located on the second floor, so you can go up the stairs.

The atmosphere was much noisier and more hectic than expected. The space was a bit noisy and there were so many people that it was difficult to concentrate on the conversation.

When taking an order, he brings out ingredients (when I went there, he brought tomatoes, although I don't remember the exact name) and explains special dishes that are not on the menu. At first, I was asked what kind of water I would like to drink. I thought it was all free and asked for mineral water, but it turned out that it was paid. Please tell me from the beginning...

Starter: We were given a pre-dinner bread and something that looked like arancini according to the number of people. There was something like meat inside, and I wasn't sure what it was, but it was delicious.

Melanzane: Fried eggplant topped with tomatoes, burrata cheese, and basil. Although it was a bit weird, it was delicious.

Trifola: Pizza topped with mushrooms, truffle cream, cheese, and arugula. I'm sure it's authentic Italian here, so it doesn't seem to have a spicy taste. There was a lot of arugula on top and it was a bit bitter, so I felt like I needed something else to catch it, but I was disappointed that it wasn't there. The dough was very chewy and delicious.

Pasta: This pasta was on the special menu. It is similar to Tagliolini pasta, but is said to use ink noodles. The noodles are very thin and resemble ramen noodles. As soon as you take a bite, you can smell the fishy smell of seafood. There were uni, shrimp, etc. It wasn't pleasant.

Daily dessert: Choose 3 desserts from the ones at the entrance and they will be cut beautifully on a tray. The blueberry pie was a little sweeter than I expected, and the apricot pie was more sour than sweet. I also ordered something like a cream puff and it was delicious.

I think the reason it received a Michelin rating was because of the slightly surprising service and the taste that was slightly not to my taste.

reviews.text:
A fresh noodle pasta restaurant you must visit before reservations become difficult! The three of us ordered and ate Caprese salad, tomato and eggplant pasta (alla norma), horse mackerel pasta, truffle pasta, and Korean beef ragu pasta. To be honest, they are all so delicious that it is difficult to choose between them, so I think it would be a good idea to order according to your personal taste.

Personally, I really liked the flavor of the truffle pasta (they seem to use good quality truffles), and the last ragu pasta I ate was also strong (‘Resinette’, a noodle made to commemorate the birth of an Italian princess😍)!!

I ordered a variety of pastas, and I liked the consideration of arranging them in an order that wouldn't spoil the taste. At first glance, the portions seem small, but they were quite generous, so one pasta per person would be fine.

There is a pasta of the day, but when I visited at 1 o'clock, the menu was sold out, and the last order was at 1:30 and the break was at 2:30, so it would be better to go a little early if possible.

The taste is comparable to that of a ristorante, but I have a small wish that the atmosphere and menu of trattorias and osterias in Italy will be maintained like they are now. Next time, I will go and try the dinner course!
